entry_conditions: Applicable to the supplied 20 Hz pd_joint_pos unstack_sort transitions in world metres, with qpos 0:9, qvel 9:18, TCP pose 18:25, red pose 25:32, blue pose 32:39 and goals 41:47 (quaternions wxyz). Provide the same two most recent causal observations used by the predecessor. Entries may be open approach, closing-in-progress or moving held lift/carry; do not initialize the phase to carry. The measured expanded-slice starts have approximately 0.080 m total finger opening, but include moving-arm states and varying TCP height. demo10200 100 is nearly pinched at roughly 0.01825 m per finger while demo10204 100 is still closing at roughly 0.02040 m per finger and -0.304 m/s finger velocities despite similar TCP height. Finger qpos/qvel, two-frame TCP/object movement, arm posture and both pad relations support causal learned phase inference. The current interface has no invocation-tag or previous-command input: object role is inferred from observations under the demonstrated red-first order, not injected from persistent API bookkeeping.
exit_conditions: For red, a useful physical exit has red remaining near its pad as measured fingers open toward 0.040 m each and TCP separates upward, then returns toward blue. Permit transfer earlier in release/retreat overlap only to a successor able to infer and finish that transition; red being geometrically at the pad is not proof of detachment. demo10204 270 is still held low, 280 is partial opening at about 0.03517 m per finger, 290 is nearly open but TCP remains low, and 310 is upward separation. Red-slice endpoints vary: demo10204 417 has open TCP near z 0.205 m while descending toward blue, versus demo10200 429 near z 0.061 m. For blue, support includes open retreat and terminal settling near TCP z 0.300 m, not only pad arrival. demo10204 625/632 remain commanded closed over the pad; 642 has near-open measured fingers but low TCP; 670 and 720 show subsequent retreat and hold. These are handoff cues, not added task-success conditions. The supplied completion contract requires only both rotated XY containment and center-z tolerance in one observation, not release, speed, clearance or a sustained hold.
overlap_role: The policy is trained on every assigned expanded slice, including acquisition subphases, release/retreat and red-to-blue approach. It is not restricted to nominal carry/place. For demo10200, shared windows with acquire_lift are [80,180), [235,430) and [440,540); for demo10204 they are [77,174), [230,418) and [434,532). These windows contain substantial moving-arm, closing and separating states. Fifteen learned ordered phases represent the complete red and blue sequence; blue approach includes the next-approach part of the red invocation. A causal two-observation recurrent encoder predicts a soft horizon phase belief rather than using slice progress or a fixed clock. Separate learned arm/gripper denoisers and measured-response training include the same transition windows. No dataset trimming, replay or scripted handoff trajectory is used.
successor_readiness: Pass the same two raw observations, object identities and world-frame goals to the successor; retain any API target bookkeeping externally. The contracted forward does not export hidden state, and there is no persistent model state to inherit. A compatible successor should reinitialize its own phase belief from these observations. It should continue +1-like opening while clearing red and not close until blue alignment supports acquisition; it must not inherit a permanent open mode. If custom integration explicitly inspects encode_history, its phase probabilities are learned, uncalibrated diagnostics, not safety certificates. Object/TCP separation and stationary-object evidence across history support release inference but do not prove contact absence. A geometrically satisfied subgoal can precede a physically useful transfer state.
failure_signatures: Watch for sampled gripper sign flicker or premature opening before object descent, fingers lagging a predicted release, red lifting again with TCP retreat, or apparent transition to blue while red still follows the TCP. Persistent divergence between native absolute joint targets and qpos beyond demonstrated tracking lag indicates a dynamics/interface mismatch, not a phase-advance signal. In demo10200 250 the second-joint target leads measured qpos by about 0.032 rad during descent, so ordinary lag must not be confused with instantaneous failure. Short causal history and qvel are imperfect evidence; held finger widths around 0.0182 m are not the attempted closed target of -0.010 m. The model has no verified contact estimator, hard gripper lock or recovery controller.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy while closing, lifting, carrying, descending or awaiting measured opening and separation if the observed state remains in the supported transition family. It can continue red release into retreat and toward the exposed blue pickup; transfer to acquire_lift within the shared open return/approach band if useful, supplying the full causal history rather than a preset phase. During blue completion it has learned open retreat toward approximately 0.300 m and terminal hold. Do not stop solely from a place-phase timer. The inference API chooses invocation duration and must separately evaluate the exact task contract; the policy has no internal stop rule. Deployment retains the fixed 16-slot action horizon and 8-action receding prefix, with continuous normalized 8D epsilon and the original action decoder. For unsupported object drops, failure to release, wrong object ordering or persistent controller mismatch, reassess and select external assistance rather than assuming this successful-trace model has a tested recovery skill.
limitations: Observed boundary/overlap evidence is training support, not a learned-policy result, hard entry threshold or proof of grasp/release. The original categorical-diffusion and semi-Markov suggestions are adapted to fixed Gaussian DDPM with a Bernoulli clean-gripper auxiliary, soft binary support, learned phase ordering and stable-event curvature; there is no categorical sampler, hard binary decoder, fixed dwell schedule or explicit duration distribution. Only two causal observations enter inference; no persistent target tag or command history can be consumed. Red-first role inference and weak geometric/motion phase labels may fail off distribution, and successful traces confound timing with state. The auxiliary response predictor is training-only and does not implement FK, IK or constraint enforcement. No failed-release or interrupted-placement recovery is established. Posterior, clearance and dwell tolerances need validation and are not measured safety bounds.
